Start the GTAPViz MCP Server for AI Assistants

Source: R/mcp_server.R
mcp_serve.Rd

Starts a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that lets AI assistants (Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code, Gemini CLI and other MCP clients) use GTAPViz on your computer: load .sl4/.har results, inspect them, and create figures and tables from plain-language requests.

You normally never call this function yourself. Run mcp_install() once and your AI app starts the server whenever it needs it.

Usage

mcp_serve(output_dir = NULL, allow_r_code = FALSE)

Arguments

output_dir

Character or NULL. Default folder for figures, tables and the session script when the AI does not choose one. If NULL (default), outputs go to an out folder next to the input folder (or to ~/GTAPViz-output for the example data).

allow_r_code

Logical. If TRUE, the AI may also run arbitrary R code in the session (tool run_r_code) for custom data manipulation. Default is FALSE, which limits the AI to GTAPViz functions.

Value

Invisibly NULL, once the AI app closes the connection.

Details

Reproducibility. Every action is executed as ordinary GTAPViz R code and appended to a session script (gtapviz_session.R, saved in the output folder). Running that script in R recreates every figure and table.

Privacy. The server runs locally and only talks to the AI app that started it. Your files are read on your computer. Results that a tool returns (summaries, numbers, preview images) become part of your conversation with the AI provider you chose, just like anything else you type there.

See also

mcp_install(), mcp_config()

Author

Pattawee Puangchit

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Started by the AI app, e.g. from a terminal:
# Rscript -e "GTAPViz::mcp_serve()"
} # }
